low_carb_diet.title: Low-carb diet
low_carb_diet.description: A low-carb diet focuses on reducing carbohydrate intake and increasing healthy fats and proteins. It may support metabolic health, weight management, and stable energy levels.

areas.energy: Low-carb diets can help stabilize energy levels and reduce blood sugar fluctuations.
areas.digestiveHealth: May improve insulin sensitivity and support metabolic health.

leafyGreens.name: Leafy greens
leafyGreens.details: Spinach, kale, lettuce, and other greens are low in carbs and high in nutrients.

meat.name: Meat
meat.details: Beef, chicken, pork, and other meats are naturally low in carbohydrates.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.details: Eggs are a versatile, low-carb source of protein and healthy fats.

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.details: Most cheeses are low in carbs and provide calcium and protein.

nuts.name: Nuts
nuts.details: Almonds, walnuts, and other nuts are low in carbs and high in healthy fats.

ketogenic_diet.title: Ketogenic diet
ketogenic_diet.description: The ketogenic diet is a very low-carb, high-fat diet that induces ketosis, a metabolic state where the body burns fat for fuel. It may support brain health, metabolic flexibility, and sustained energy.

areas.energy: Ketogenic diets can provide stable energy by relying on fat as the primary fuel source.
areas.digestiveHealth: May improve metabolic flexibility and support blood sugar regulation.
areas.mind: Ketones produced during ketosis may support brain health and cognitive function.

avocado.name: Avocado
avocado.details: Avocados are high in healthy fats and fiber, and very low in carbs.

coconutOil.name: Coconut oil
coconutOil.details: Coconut oil is a source of medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs) that support ketosis.

fattyFish.name: Fatty fish
fattyFish.details: Salmon, mackerel, and sardines are rich in omega-3 fats and low in carbs.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.details: Eggs are a staple in ketogenic diets for their protein and fat content.

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.details: Cheese is low in carbs and high in fat, making it ideal for keto.

berberine.title: Berberine for blood sugar, lipids and metabolism
berberine.description: Berberine is a plant compound that may support blood sugar balance, blood lipids, gut health, and metabolism. Often used as a supplement for insulin resistance, to improve gut flora, and may also inhibit Helicobacter pylori.

areas.digestiveHealth: Supports gut flora balance and health. May inhibit Helicobacter pylori.
areas.cardioFitness: May improve blood lipid profile (cholesterol and triglycerides).
areas.energy: Supports metabolism and fat burning. May help regulate blood sugar levels.

brown_fat_cool_home.title: Brown fat and a cool home environment
brown_fat_cool_home.description: Brown fat helps the body burn energy and generate heat. Spending time in a cool indoor environment, ideally below 21°C (70°F), can stimulate brown fat activity and increase energy expenditure. Lowering the temperature at home occasionally may support metabolism and metabolic health.

areas.energy: Activation of brown fat increases energy expenditure and may support better metabolic health.

colorful_vegetables_anthocyanins.title: Eat a variety of colorful vegetables
colorful_vegetables_anthocyanins.description: Eating vegetables in a variety of colors, especially dark and red ones rich in anthocyanins, provides a broad spectrum of antioxidants and phytonutrients. Anthocyanins, found in foods like blueberries, red cabbage, and beets, have been shown to support heart health, reduce inflammation, and protect cells from oxidative stress. Vary your vegetable colors to maximize health benefits.

areas.nutrition: Colorful vegetables provide different vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants that strengthen the immune system and promote overall health.

eat_colorful_veggies.title: Eat colorful vegetables
eat_colorful_veggies.description: Eating vegetables in a variety of colors provides a broad spectrum of antioxidants and nutrients. Vary the colors on your plate to support digestion and immune function.

areas.digestiveHealth: Colorful vegetables support gut health and digestion.
areas.immuneSupport: Different colors provide different antioxidants that strengthen the immune system.

redVeggies.name: Red vegetables (tomato, bell pepper, beetroot)
redVeggies.details: Red vegetables are rich in lycopene and anthocyanins, supporting heart health and immunity.

orangeVeggies.name: Orange vegetables (carrot, pumpkin, sweet potato)
orangeVeggies.details: Orange vegetables contain beta-carotene, which converts to vitamin A and supports vision and skin.

yellowVeggies.name: Yellow vegetables (yellow pepper, corn)
yellowVeggies.details: Yellow vegetables are high in lutein and zeaxanthin, supporting eye health.

greenVeggies.name: Green vegetables (spinach, broccoli, peas)
greenVeggies.details: Green vegetables contain chlorophyll, folate, and magnesium, supporting energy and nervous system.

bluePurpleVeggies.name: Blue/purple vegetables (blueberries, red cabbage, eggplant)
bluePurpleVeggies.details: Blue and purple vegetables are rich in anthocyanins, protecting cells and supporting brain function.

vitamin_d.title: Vitamin D
vitamin_d.description: Vitamin D levels can vary based on factors such as sun exposure, diet, and geographic location. Pairing D3 with complementary vitamin K2 helps route calcium to bones and protects soft tissues. Consider adding magnesium bisglycinate to support vitamin D activation and efficient calcium uptake.

areas.energy: Vitamin D supports mitochondrial function and cellular energy production by regulating calcium homeostasis.
areas.immuneSupport: Vitamin D modulates both innate and adaptive immune responses, with low levels associated with increased infection susceptibility.
areas.strength: Vitamin D is critical for muscle strength and function through calcium regulation and muscle protein synthesis pathways.
areas.nervousSystem: Vitamin D influences neurotransmitter production and has neuroprotective effects in the central nervous system.

fattyFish.name: Fatty fish (salmon, mackerel, sardines)
fattyFish.details: Aim for a 120 g serving of salmon or mackerel 2-3 times per week (~400-600 IU vitamin D).

eggYolks.name: Egg yolks
eggYolks.details: Two egg yolks supply roughly 80-100 IU vitamin D.

fortifiedDairy.name: Fortified dairy or plant milks
fortifiedDairy.details: A 250 ml glass of fortified milk or plant milk delivers about 100-130 IU vitamin D.

mushrooms.name: Sun-exposed mushrooms
mushrooms.details: 100 g sun-exposed mushrooms can provide roughly 400 IU vitamin D.

vitamin_e_antioxidant_support.title: Vitamin E for antioxidant defense
vitamin_e_antioxidant_support.description: Vitamin E shields cell membranes from oxidative stress and supports cardiovascular resilience. Mixed tocopherols and tocotrienols cover a wider spectrum than alpha-tocopherol alone, making them useful when inflammatory or lipid stress is high. Combining with carotenoids like astaxanthin offers complementary membrane protection. Large doses of isolated alpha-tocopherol can crowd out other E forms, so stay near label guidance unless you are using mixed complexes.

areas.immuneSupport: Vitamin E enhances immune cell signaling and protects lipids in cell membranes from peroxidation.
areas.cardioFitness: Adequate vitamin E helps maintain endothelial function and balances oxidative load during exercise.
areas.energy: By preserving mitochondrial membranes, vitamin E supports efficient energy production under stress.

coq10.title: Mitokondrienäring
coq10.description: Vissa näringsämnen är involverade i mitokondriella processer relaterade till cellulär energiproduktion.

areas.energy: CoQ10 spelar en kritisk roll i den mitokondriella elektrontransportkedjan, vilket är avgörande för cellulär energiproduktion.
areas.immuneSupport: CoQ10 har antioxidantegenskaper som hjälper till att skydda celler från oxidativ stress och stödjer immunsystemets funktion.

coq10.analyzePrompt: Analysera bilden och bestäm mitokondriens behov av stöd.

organMeats.name: Organ meats (heart, liver)
organMeats.details: An 85 g serving of beef heart or liver supplies around 10-15 mg CoQ10.

fattyFish.name: Fatty fish (sardines, mackerel)
fattyFish.details: 120 g sardines or mackerel delivers roughly 6 mg CoQ10.

beef.name: Beef and bison
beef.details: 120 g lean beef offers about 3 mg CoQ10.

spinach.name: Spinach
spinach.details: 1 cup cooked spinach (~180 g) provides about 2 mg CoQ10.

broccoli.name: Broccoli
broccoli.details: 1 cup steamed broccoli (~150 g) yields roughly 1 mg CoQ10.

cellular_energy_nad.title: NAD+
cellular_energy_nad.description: NAD+ (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide) is a critical coenzyme found in every cell of the body. It plays a key role in cellular energy metabolism, DNA repair, and maintaining overall cellular health. Precursors such as NMN, NR, or foundational niacin can sustain NAD+ levels when direct supplementation is not preferred.

areas.energy: NAD+ is essential for the mitochondrial processes that generate ATP, the primary energy currency of the cell.
areas.nervousSystem: NAD+ supports the nervous system by aiding in cellular repair and protecting neurons from oxidative stress.
areas.immuneSupport: NAD+ contributes to immune function by supporting cellular metabolism and repair mechanisms vital for immune cells.

cellular_energy_nad.analyzePrompt: Analyze the user's NAD+ levels and suggest strategies to optimize cellular energy metabolism.

sleep_timing_circadian.title: Sleep timing and circadian rhythm
sleep_timing_circadian.description: Synchronizing sleep with the body's natural circadian rhythm optimizes sleep quality and recovery. Consistent sleep and wake times help regulate hormone production and metabolism.

areas.sleepQuality: Regular sleep rhythm improves sleep quality by strengthening the body's natural melatonin production.
areas.immuneSupport: Circadian synchronization supports immune function by optimizing the body's natural defense cycles.
areas.energy: Consistent sleep schedule regulates energy levels and reduces daytime fatigue.
areas.longevity: Stable circadian timing supports long-term metabolic, hormonal, and cognitive resilience, which are key factors for healthy aging.

calm_alertness_ltheanine.title: L-Theanine for calm focus
calm_alertness_ltheanine.description: L-Theanine is an amino acid naturally found in green tea. It promotes relaxation without drowsiness and enhances focus by increasing alpha brain waves and balancing neurotransmitters like GABA, dopamine, and serotonin.

areas.mind: L-Theanine improves concentration and attention while reducing stress and promoting a state of calm alertness.

neurotransmitter_ltyrosine.title: L-Tyrosine for mental performance
neurotransmitter_ltyrosine.description: L-Tyrosine is an amino acid that serves as a precursor to dopamine, norepinephrine, and adrenaline. It supports cognitive function, focus, and mental performance, especially during stressful situations.

areas.mind: L-Tyrosine improves concentration, attention, and cognitive performance by increasing the production of key neurotransmitters.

maintain_hydration.title: Maintain hydration
maintain_hydration.description: Consistent daily fluid intake supports circulation, temperature regulation, and immune defense function. Adequate hydration is fundamental for all bodily functions.

areas.immuneSupport: Hydration supports immune defense by promoting lymph circulation and nutrient transport to cells.
areas.energy: Adequate fluid maintains energy levels and reduces fatigue by optimizing cellular metabolism.
areas.cardioFitness: Hydration improves cardiovascular performance by maintaining blood volume and oxygen transport.

electrolytes_balance.title: Electrolytes for fluid balance and performance
electrolytes_balance.description: Electrolytes such as sodium, potassium, and magnesium help regulate fluid balance, nerve signaling, muscle contraction, and blood pressure. When you sweat a lot, train hard, or drink large amounts of plain water without replacing minerals, low electrolyte status can contribute to fatigue, headaches, reduced performance, or muscle cramps. For sodium, mineral-rich salt or broth is often more relevant than simply increasing regular table salt, especially since high intake of ordinary table salt can contribute to elevated blood pressure in salt-sensitive individuals.

areas.energy: Electrolytes help maintain cellular fluid balance and nerve-muscle function, which supports stable energy and reduces fatigue.
areas.cardioFitness: During exercise and heat exposure, adequate electrolytes help preserve blood volume, hydration status, and physical performance.
areas.nervousSystem: Sodium and potassium are essential for nerve impulses, while magnesium supports normal neuromuscular relaxation and signaling.

mineralWater.name: Mineral water
mineralWater.details: Mineral-rich water can provide sodium, magnesium, and other electrolytes, especially after sweating.

coconutWater.name: Coconut water
coconutWater.details: A glass of coconut water provides potassium and fluid, useful after heat or light training.

potatoes.name: Potatoes or root vegetables
potatoes.details: Potatoes are rich in potassium, one of the key minerals involved in muscle and nerve function.

saltedMeals.name: Mineral-rich salt, salted meals, or broth
saltedMeals.details: Mineral-rich salt or a properly salted broth can help restore sodium losses after prolonged sweating. Regular table salt should not be overused, since higher intake can contribute to elevated blood pressure in some people.

dental_health_basics.title: Dental health basics
dental_health_basics.description: Basic oral care is one of the highest-return health habits. Regular brushing, cleaning between the teeth, reducing frequent sugar exposure, and supporting a healthier oral microbiome can lower caries risk, protect the gums, and preserve teeth long term. Frequent snacking is a major problem because the teeth are exposed to repeated acid attacks and less time to recover between meals, which raises caries risk even when the food itself does not seem extreme. Good chewing function and low oral inflammation also support digestion and overall health.

areas.immuneSupport: Healthier gums and lower oral inflammation reduce chronic immune burden and help maintain a more balanced inflammatory state. Bleeding gums can also make it easier for oral bacteria and inflammatory compounds to enter the bloodstream, and poor gum health has been associated with a higher long-term risk of cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease.
areas.digestiveHealth: Good dental health supports chewing, saliva production, and the first stage of digestion while reducing problems linked to an unhealthy oral microbiome.

vitamin_c_immunity.title: Vitamin C for immunity
vitamin_c_immunity.description: Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin found in fruits and vegetables. It is a powerful antioxidant that supports the immune system and protects cells from oxidative stress.

areas.immuneSupport: Vitamin C strengthens immune defense by supporting white blood cells and increasing the body's resistance to infections.

citrusFruits.name: Citrus fruits (oranges, grapefruit, lemon)
citrusFruits.details: One medium orange (~130 g) yields about 70 mg vitamin C.

berries.name: Berries (strawberries, blackcurrants)
berries.details: 1 cup mixed berries (~150 g) supplies roughly 80 mg vitamin C.

bellPeppers.name: Bell peppers
bellPeppers.details: Half a cup raw red pepper (~75 g) gives about 95 mg vitamin C.

kiwi.name: Kiwi fruit
kiwi.details: One large kiwi (~75 g) provides about 70 mg vitamin C.

fermentedCabbage.name: Fermented cabbage (sauerkraut, kimchi)
fermentedCabbage.details: Half a cup sauerkraut (~70 g) offers around 20 mg vitamin C.

echinacea_herbs.title: Echinacea for immune support
echinacea_herbs.description: Echinacea is a flowering plant traditionally used to support immune function. It contains active compounds that may help the body's natural defense mechanisms and has been studied for its potential to reduce the duration and severity of common colds.

areas.immuneSupport: Echinacea stimulates immune cell activity and may help the body respond more effectively to infections and support overall immune resilience.

calming_glycine.title: Calming amino acids
calming_glycine.description: Glycine is an amino acid that acts as a neurotransmitter in the central nervous system. It has been studied for its calming effects and its role in promoting relaxation and better sleep.

areas.nervousSystem: Glycine acts as an inhibitory neurotransmitter, helping to calm the nervous system and reduce stress.
areas.sleepQuality: Glycine has been shown to improve sleep quality by promoting relaxation and regulating body temperature.
areas.immuneSupport: Glycine supports immune function by reducing inflammation and promoting cellular repair.

boneBroth.name: Bone broth
boneBroth.details: A 250 ml cup of long-simmered bone broth gives about 2-3 g glycine.

collagenCuts.name: Collagen-rich cuts (brisket, shank)
collagenCuts.details: 120 g braised brisket or shank supplies roughly 3 g glycine-rich collagen.

skinOnPoultry.name: Skin-on poultry
skinOnPoultry.details: 100 g roasted chicken with skin provides about 2 g glycine.

porkRinds.name: Pork rinds or cracklings
porkRinds.details: 30 g pork rinds contain around 2.5 g glycine.

legumes.name: Legumes (soy, beans, lentils)
legumes.details: 1 cup cooked soybeans or lentils (~180 g) offers about 2 g glycine.

muscle_leucine.title: Leucine for muscle synthesis
muscle_leucine.description: Leucine is the primary branched-chain amino acid that activates mTOR, the master regulator of muscle protein synthesis. Getting sufficient leucine, especially post-workout, is critical for building and maintaining muscle mass.

areas.strength: Leucine directly activates mTOR signaling, triggering muscle protein synthesis and recovery. A single dose of 3-5g post-workout stimulates muscle repair and growth by reducing protein breakdown.

beef.name: Beef
beef.details: 120 g cooked lean beef provides about 2.5-3 g leucine.

chicken.name: Chicken breast
chicken.details: 120 g cooked chicken breast contains roughly 2-2.5 g leucine.

fish.name: Fish (salmon, tuna)
fish.details: 120 g cooked fish supplies about 2-2.5 g leucine.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.details: 3 large eggs provide about 1.8-2 g leucine.

dairyProducts.name: Greek yogurt or cottage cheese
dairyProducts.details: 150 g Greek yogurt contains approximately 2-2.5 g leucine.

wheyProtein.name: Whey protein isolate
wheyProtein.details: 30 g whey protein powder delivers roughly 2.5-3 g leucine.

bcaa_complex.title: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs)
bcaa_complex.description: BCAAs—leucine, isoleucine, and valine—are essential amino acids that bypass liver metabolism and go directly to muscle. They support muscle protein synthesis, reduce fatigue, and aid recovery. The optimal ratio is roughly 2:1:1 (leucine:isoleucine:valine).

areas.strength: The BCAA ratio of 2:1:1 maximizes muscle protein synthesis and recovery. Leucine triggers mTOR, while isoleucine and valine reduce muscle breakdown — helping maintain mass during intense training blocks.
areas.cardioFitness: BCAAs reduce central fatigue, spare muscle glycogen during endurance sessions, and accelerate recovery between workouts by reducing delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS).

beef.name: Lean beef
beef.details: 120 g lean beef contains a balanced BCAA profile (~5.5 g total BCAAs).

chicken.name: Chicken
chicken.details: 120 g chicken breast has about 4.5-5 g total BCAAs.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.details: 3 large eggs supply roughly 4.5-5 g BCAAs.

dairyProducts.name: Whey protein
dairyProducts.details: 30 g whey protein provides about 6-7 g total BCAAs in the optimal 2:1:1 ratio.

arginine_pump.title: Arginine for blood flow and pump
arginine_pump.description: Arginine is a semi-essential amino acid that boosts nitric oxide (NO) production, increasing blood flow, nutrient delivery, and the muscle pump. It's especially effective taken pre-workout to enhance performance and vascularity.

areas.cardioFitness: Arginine increases nitric oxide production, which relaxes blood vessel walls, improving blood flow and cardiovascular efficiency.
areas.strength: Better blood flow enhances oxygen and nutrient delivery to muscles during training, supporting performance, strength, and the muscle pump.

pumpkinSeeds.name: Pumpkin seeds
pumpkinSeeds.details: 30 g pumpkin seeds provide about 2-2.5 g arginine.

sesameSeeds.name: Sesame seeds
sesameSeeds.details: 30 g sesame seeds contain roughly 1.5-2 g arginine.

almonds.name: Almonds
almonds.details: 30 g almonds supply about 1-1.5 g arginine.

pecans.name: Pecans
pecans.details: 30 g pecans provide roughly 1-1.2 g arginine.

watermelon.name: Watermelon
watermelon.details: A slice of watermelon (200 g) contains about 250-350 mg arginine, plus citrulline which converts to arginine.

whey_protein.title: Whey Protein for muscle growth
whey_protein.description: Whey protein is a fast-digesting, complete protein derived from milk. It contains all essential amino acids, with an exceptionally high leucine content — the key amino acid that triggers muscle protein synthesis. Taking 25–30 g of whey post-workout maximizes the anabolic window and supports muscle repair and growth.

areas.strength: Whey delivers a rapid leucine spike (~2.5 g per 30 g serving) that activates the mTOR pathway, maximizing muscle protein synthesis and recovery after resistance training.
areas.cardioFitness: Adequate protein intake supports endurance performance by preserving muscle mass during long training blocks and accelerating recovery between sessions.

chickenBreast.name: Chicken breast
chickenBreast.details: 150 g chicken breast provides about 45 g protein with ~3.5 g leucine.

tuna.name: Tuna
tuna.details: 150 g canned tuna delivers ~35 g protein with ~3 g leucine.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.details: 3 large eggs supply ~18 g protein with ~1.5 g leucine.

greekYogurt.name: Greek yogurt
greekYogurt.details: 200 g Greek yogurt provides ~20 g protein with ~1.8 g leucine.

cottageCheese.name: Cottage cheese
cottageCheese.details: 200 g cottage cheese contains ~25 g protein with ~2 g leucine.

homocysteine_methylation_cardio.title: Methylation and cardiovascular support (homocysteine)
homocysteine_methylation_cardio.description: Homocysteine is a sulfur-containing amino acid formed during methionine metabolism. When chronically elevated, it is associated with higher cardiovascular risk and poorer vascular function. A practical strategy is to support methylation and redox balance through nutrients such as TMG (trimethylglycine), B vitamins (especially B6, folate/B9, and B12), glycine, NAC, and green tea catechins (EGCG; sometimes written as ICG by mistake), alongside folate-rich and choline-rich foods.

areas.cardioFitness: Keeping homocysteine in a healthy range supports endothelial function, nitric oxide signaling, and vascular resilience. TMG donates methyl groups for remethylation pathways, folate/B12 support homocysteine recycling, and B6 supports transsulfuration. NAC and glycine also support glutathione status and oxidative stress control.
areas.longevity: Methylation efficiency influences DNA maintenance, detox capacity, and inflammatory tone over time. Combining methyl donors (TMG, folate, B12) with cofactors such as B6 and glycine support helps balance one-carbon metabolism and can be useful in long-term prevention strategies.

beets.name: Beets
beets.details: Beets are naturally rich in betaine (TMG precursor), which can help support homocysteine remethylation.

spinach.name: Spinach
spinach.details: Spinach provides folate needed for methylation pathways tied to homocysteine metabolism.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.details: Egg yolks contain choline, a key methyl donor supporting liver and methylation function.

broccoli.name: Broccoli
broccoli.details: Broccoli contributes folate and sulfur compounds that support detoxification and redox balance.

chickpeas.name: Chickpeas
chickpeas.details: Chickpeas are a practical source of vitamin B6 and folate, both relevant for homocysteine metabolism.

salmon.name: Salmon
salmon.details: Salmon supplies methionine, B vitamins, and omega-3s that support cardiovascular health when balanced with methylation cofactors.

greenTea.name: Green tea
greenTea.details: Green tea catechins (especially EGCG) provide antioxidant support relevant to vascular health.

collagen.title: Collagen for connective tissue
collagen.description: Collagen is a structural protein that supports joints, tendons, ligaments, skin, and bone matrix. Collagen peptides can be a practical way to support connective tissue resilience, especially together with a protein-rich diet and adequate vitamin C intake.

areas.strength: Collagen provides amino acids such as glycine and proline that support connective tissue structure in joints, tendons, ligaments, and bones.

boneBroth.name: Bone broth
boneBroth.details: 300 ml long-simmered bone broth can provide a few grams of collagen-derived amino acids depending on preparation.

collagenCuts.name: Collagen-rich cuts (brisket, shank)
collagenCuts.details: 120 g braised brisket or shank supplies roughly 3 g glycine-rich collagen.

skinOnPoultry.name: Chicken with skin or fish skin
skinOnPoultry.details: A serving with skin contributes collagen-rich connective tissue proteins.

citrulline_bloodflow_gut.title: Citrulline for blood flow and gut support
citrulline_bloodflow_gut.description: L-citrulline is an amino acid that can be converted into arginine and help raise nitric oxide production. It is best known for supporting circulation, endothelial function, and blood flow, which is why it is often used for cardiovascular performance and pump-related effects in training. For gut health, it is interesting because this same circulation support may help blood flow to the intestinal lining and help maintain barrier integrity during physiological stress, heavy training, or recovery. It is a more specialized supplement than fiber and probiotics, but can be relevant when the goal is to support both vascular function and mucosal resilience.

areas.digestiveHealth: By supporting arginine and nitric oxide availability, citrulline may help circulation and recovery processes in the intestinal mucosa.
areas.cardioFitness: Citrulline is most known for increasing nitric oxide availability, which can support endothelial function, blood flow, and cardiovascular performance.

watermelon.name: Watermelon
watermelon.details: Watermelon is the best-known food source of citrulline, with the highest concentrations typically found in the white rind close to the peel.

cantaloupe.name: Cantaloupe and other melons
cantaloupe.details: Other melons also contain citrulline, though usually in smaller amounts than watermelon.

cucumber.name: Cucumber
cucumber.details: Cucumber contains small amounts of citrulline and can modestly contribute as part of a plant-rich diet.

glutathione.title: Glutathione for antioxidant defense
glutathione.description: Glutathione is one of the body's most important intracellular antioxidants. It is built from the amino acids glycine, glutamate, and cysteine, and helps neutralize reactive oxygen species, supports liver detoxification pathways, and protects cells during stress, inflammation, and high metabolic demand. Direct glutathione can be used, but many people also support glutathione status through precursors such as NAC. Glycine availability can matter for glutathione synthesis, while glutamate is one of the core building blocks already required in the molecule itself.

areas.immuneSupport: Glutathione helps immune cells manage oxidative stress and maintain balanced inflammatory signaling.
areas.energy: By protecting mitochondria and other cell structures from oxidative damage, glutathione supports efficient cellular energy production.

broccoli.name: Broccoli and other cruciferous vegetables
broccoli.details: Cruciferous vegetables provide sulfur compounds that support the body's own glutathione production.

avocado.name: Avocado
avocado.details: Avocado provides antioxidant nutrients that can help maintain glutathione status.

spinach.name: Spinach
spinach.details: Spinach contributes folate and plant antioxidants that support cellular redox balance.

breathwork_parasympathetic.title: Breathwork techniques
breathwork_parasympathetic.description: Breathwork is a powerful tool for activating the parasympathetic nervous system, reducing stress, and promoting relaxation. Different breathing techniques can be used for specific outcomes such as calm, focus, or better sleep.

areas.nervousSystem: Controlled breathing directly activates the parasympathetic nervous system, reducing stress hormones and promoting relaxation.
areas.immuneSupport: Regular breathwork can improve immune function by reducing chronic stress and promoting better sleep and recovery.
areas.energy: Proper breathing techniques enhance oxygen utilization and energy levels throughout the day.

box_breathing.title: Box breathing
box_breathing.description: Box breathing (also called square breathing) is a technique where you inhale, hold, exhale, and hold again for equal counts (typically 4-4-4-4). It's excellent for rapid stress relief and focus.

areas.nervousSystem: Box breathing creates a balanced rhythm that quickly activates the parasympathetic nervous system.
areas.immuneSupport: Regular practice helps reduce cortisol levels and supports immune resilience.

4_7_8_breathing.title: 4-7-8 breathing
4_7_8_breathing.description: The 4-7-8 technique involves inhaling for 4 counts, holding for 7 counts, and exhaling for 8 counts. It's particularly effective for relaxation and sleep preparation.

areas.nervousSystem: The extended exhale activates the vagus nerve, promoting deep relaxation and reducing anxiety.
areas.sleepQuality: This technique is highly effective for preparing the body and mind for sleep, improving sleep quality.

alternate_nostril_breathing.title: Alternate nostril breathing
alternate_nostril_breathing.description: Nadi Shodhana (alternate nostril breathing) involves breathing through one nostril at a time in a controlled pattern. It balances the nervous system and enhances mental clarity.

areas.nervousSystem: This technique balances the left and right sides of the nervous system, promoting harmony and calm.
areas.mind: Alternate nostril breathing enhances mental clarity and concentration by balancing brain hemispheres.

diaphragmatic_breathing.title: Diaphragmatic breathing
diaphragmatic_breathing.description: Also called belly breathing or deep breathing, this technique focuses on breathing deeply into the abdomen rather than the chest. It's fundamental to all breathwork practices.

areas.nervousSystem: Deep diaphragmatic breathing significantly reduces stress and anxiety by activating the relaxation response.
areas.energy: Proper oxygenation through diaphragmatic breathing improves energy levels and mental clarity.

sleep_optimization_recovery.title: Sleep optimization for recovery
sleep_optimization_recovery.description: Quality sleep is fundamental for physical recovery, immune function, mental clarity, and overall health. Sleep optimization involves multiple factors including duration, consistency, environment, and pre-sleep routines.

areas.nervousSystem: Quality sleep supports nervous system recovery and balance between sympathetic and parasympathetic systems.
areas.immuneSupport: Sleep is crucial for immune function and the body's ability to fight infections and heal.
areas.energy: Adequate sleep restores energy levels and optimizes the body's metabolic processes.
areas.cardioFitness: Sleep supports cardiovascular health by regulating blood pressure and heart rate.
areas.sleepQuality: Optimized sleep habits improve sleep quality, deep sleep, and REM sleep for maximum recovery.

sleep_duration_consistency.title: Sleep duration and consistency
sleep_duration_consistency.description: Getting 7-9 hours of consistent sleep each night is crucial for nervous system recovery, hormonal balance, and cellular repair. Maintaining a consistent sleep schedule helps regulate your circadian rhythm.

areas.sleepQuality: Consistent 7-9 hours of sleep allows for complete sleep cycles, including deep sleep and REM sleep necessary for memory consolidation and emotional processing.
areas.energy: Adequate sleep duration directly impacts energy levels, cognitive function, and physical performance throughout the day.

sleep_environment_optimization.title: Sleep environment optimization
sleep_environment_optimization.description: Creating an optimal sleep environment is essential for quality sleep. This includes darkness, cool temperature, quiet conditions, and comfortable bedding that support restorative sleep.

areas.sleepQuality: A dark, cool (60-67°F), quiet environment promotes melatonin production and deeper sleep cycles.
areas.nervousSystem: An optimized sleep environment reduces external stressors and allows the nervous system to fully relax and recover.

sleep_hygiene_practices.title: Sleep hygiene practices
sleep_hygiene_practices.description: Sleep hygiene encompasses daily habits that promote better sleep, such as avoiding caffeine in the afternoon, limiting screen time before bed, and maintaining regular exercise routines.

areas.sleepQuality: Good sleep hygiene practices remove barriers to quality sleep and create conditions for deeper, more restorative rest.
areas.immuneSupport: Quality sleep from good hygiene practices strengthens immune function and supports the body's ability to fight infections.

pre_sleep_wind_down.title: Pre-sleep wind-down routine
pre_sleep_wind_down.description: A structured wind-down routine 30-60 minutes before bed signals to your body that it's time to sleep. This can include relaxation techniques, light reading, meditation, or gentle stretching.

areas.sleepQuality: A proper wind-down routine helps transition the nervous system from wakefulness to sleep, promoting faster sleep onset and deeper sleep.
areas.nervousSystem: Pre-sleep relaxation techniques activate the parasympathetic nervous system, preparing the body for restorative sleep.

sunlight_circadian.title: Morning sunlight exposure
sunlight_circadian.description: Exposure to natural sunlight, especially within 30-60 minutes of waking, is crucial for regulating circadian rhythm and optimizing sleep-wake cycles. Morning light suppresses melatonin and signals the start of the day.

areas.sleepQuality: Morning sunlight exposure helps set your circadian clock, improving sleep quality and making it easier to fall asleep at night.
areas.nervousSystem: Natural light exposure regulates the nervous system by synchronizing circadian rhythms and supporting balanced cortisol production.
areas.energy: Morning sunlight boosts alertness and energy levels throughout the day by signaling to your body that it's time to be awake.
areas.immuneSupport: Regular circadian rhythm from sunlight exposure supports immune function and overall health.

cold_exposure_ans.title: Cold exposure therapy
cold_exposure_ans.description: Deliberate cold exposure, such as cold showers, ice baths, or cold plunges, activates the sympathetic nervous system and builds stress resilience. Regular cold exposure improves immune function, increases energy, and enhances mental clarity.

areas.nervousSystem: Cold exposure trains the nervous system to handle stress by activating and then balancing the sympathetic and parasympathetic responses.
areas.immuneSupport: Regular cold exposure has been shown to increase white blood cell count and strengthen immune function.
areas.energy: Cold exposure boosts dopamine and norepinephrine levels, leading to increased alertness, energy, and mood elevation.

meditation_mindfulness.title: Meditation and mindfulness
meditation_mindfulness.description: Regular meditation and mindfulness practices train the mind to stay present and reduce stress. These practices activate the parasympathetic nervous system, improve emotional regulation, and enhance cognitive function.

areas.nervousSystem: Meditation activates the parasympathetic nervous system, reducing stress hormones like cortisol and promoting deep relaxation and nervous system recovery.
areas.immuneSupport: Regular meditation has been shown to reduce inflammation, strengthen immune response, and improve overall health markers.
areas.mind: Mindfulness practices improve attention span, working memory, and cognitive flexibility by strengthening neural pathways associated with focus and awareness.
areas.longevity: Lower chronic stress and better autonomic balance are associated with reduced allostatic load and improved long-term healthspan.

ikigai_purpose_longevity.title: Purpose and longevity
ikigai_purpose_longevity.description: Finding a sense of purpose is a key driver of longevity, linked to lower disease risk and slower cognitive decline. Build your own Ikigai by identifying what you love, what you are good at, and what the world needs, then turn that overlap into small daily actions.

areas.philosophy: Ikigai is a philosophical framework that helps align values, strengths, and contribution into meaningful daily action.
areas.mind: A clear purpose improves motivation, emotional resilience, and cognitive engagement over time.
areas.longevity: People with a stronger sense of purpose tend to show lower chronic disease risk, better health behaviors, and a longer healthspan.

stoic_dichotomy_control.title: Stoic dichotomy of control
stoic_dichotomy_control.description: Write down one current stressor and split it into two lists: what you can control and what you cannot. Act only on the controllable list today.

areas.philosophy: This is a practical philosophical model for reducing noise and improving intentional action.
areas.nervousSystem: Shifting focus to controllable factors lowers perceived stress load and helps autonomic balance.

memento_mori_priority.title: Memento mori for priorities
memento_mori_priority.description: Use mortality awareness as clarity, not fear. Ask: If this week mattered deeply, what would I stop doing and what would I start?

areas.philosophy: Memento mori sharpens attention toward what is meaningful instead of what is merely urgent.
areas.longevity: Clear priorities improve long-term consistency in habits that protect healthspan.

virtue_before_mood.title: Virtue before mood
virtue_before_mood.description: Choose one virtue for today (courage, patience, honesty, discipline) and define one concrete action that expresses it.

areas.philosophy: Virtue ethics translates abstract values into concrete behavior.
areas.mind: Value-based action reduces decision fatigue and improves self-trust.

amor_fati_reframe.title: Amor fati reframe
amor_fati_reframe.description: When something goes wrong, ask: How can this event train a useful skill in me? Reframe setbacks into deliberate practice.

areas.philosophy: Amor fati means relating to reality as training material, not an enemy.
areas.nervousSystem: Cognitive reframing can reduce threat perception and calm stress reactivity.
areas.mind: Reframing adversity strengthens psychological flexibility and resilience.

philosophical_journaling.title: Philosophical journaling
philosophical_journaling.description: Each evening, answer three prompts: What did I do well? Where did I miss my values? What is one better choice tomorrow?

areas.philosophy: Reflection turns philosophy into a repeated practice rather than a theory.
areas.mind: Structured reflection improves metacognition and emotional regulation.
areas.longevity: Small daily course-corrections improve long-term behavior quality.

philosophical_walk.title: Philosophical walk
philosophical_walk.description: Take a 20-minute walk without audio input and think through one guiding question about your current life direction.

areas.philosophy: Walking contemplation has long been used to clarify judgment and priorities.
areas.mind: Low-stimulus walking can restore attention and improve cognitive clarity.
areas.nervousSystem: Slow walking with intentional breathing supports parasympathetic activation.

nature_parasympathetic.title: Time in nature
nature_parasympathetic.description: Spending time in natural environments activates the parasympathetic nervous system and reduces stress. Forest bathing (Shinrin-yoku) and exposure to natural settings have been shown to lower cortisol, reduce blood pressure, and improve overall well-being.

areas.nervousSystem: Nature exposure activates the parasympathetic nervous system, reducing stress hormones and promoting relaxation and recovery.
areas.immuneSupport: Time in nature has been shown to boost natural killer cell activity and strengthen immune function.
areas.energy: Natural environments restore mental energy, reduce fatigue, and improve mood through exposure to natural light and fresh air.

hrv_recovery_monitoring.title: HRV and recovery monitoring
hrv_recovery_monitoring.description: Heart Rate Variability (HRV) is a key metric for tracking nervous system balance and recovery status. Monitoring HRV helps optimize training intensity, prevent overtraining, and ensure adequate recovery between workouts.

areas.nervousSystem: HRV reflects the balance between sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system activity, indicating stress and recovery levels.
areas.immuneSupport: Low HRV can indicate increased inflammation and reduced immune function, while higher HRV suggests better recovery and immune resilience.
areas.energy: HRV tracking helps identify when the body needs rest, preventing fatigue and optimizing energy management.
areas.cardioFitness: Monitoring HRV helps optimize cardiovascular training by ensuring adequate recovery between high-intensity sessions.
areas.strength: HRV data guides training decisions, helping prevent overtraining and optimize muscle recovery and performance gains.
areas.longevity: Tracking recovery helps maintain sustainable training and lower chronic stress burden, both important for long-term health and functional aging.

social_connection_vagal.title: Social connection and vagal tone
social_connection_vagal.description: Positive social interactions and meaningful relationships activate the vagus nerve and strengthen parasympathetic tone. Social connection is essential for nervous system regulation, emotional well-being, and overall health.

areas.nervousSystem: Positive social interactions activate the vagus nerve, improving heart rate variability and promoting parasympathetic nervous system activation.
areas.immuneSupport: Strong social connections have been shown to reduce inflammation, strengthen immune function, and increase longevity.
areas.energy: Meaningful relationships and social support reduce stress and improve energy levels by lowering cortisol and enhancing emotional resilience.

calming_music_waves.title: Calming music and sound therapy
calming_music_waves.description: Listening to calming music, binaural beats, or nature sounds can reduce stress, lower heart rate, and activate the parasympathetic nervous system. Sound therapy has been used for centuries to promote relaxation and healing.

areas.nervousSystem: Calming music and sound therapy activate the parasympathetic nervous system, reducing stress hormones and promoting deep relaxation.
areas.sleepQuality: Listening to calming sounds before bed can improve sleep onset, increase deep sleep duration, and enhance overall sleep quality.
areas.mind: Certain frequencies like binaural beats and nature sounds can enhance concentration, reduce mental fatigue, and improve cognitive performance.

adaptogenic_herbs.title: Adaptogenic herbs
adaptogenic_herbs.description: Adaptogenic herbs help the body adapt to stress and promote balance. They support energy, resilience, and overall wellbeing.

areas.nervousSystem: Adaptogenic herbs support the nervous system by modulating the stress response and promoting mental and physical resilience.

medicinal_mushrooms.title: Medicinal mushrooms
medicinal_mushrooms.description: Medicinal mushrooms are traditionally used to support immunity, energy, the nervous system, and cognitive function. Different mushrooms have different strengths, so the best choice depends on your goal.

areas.immuneSupport: Many medicinal mushrooms contain beta-glucans and other bioactive compounds that may support balanced immune function.
areas.mind: Some medicinal mushrooms may also support focus, mental clarity, and nervous system recovery.

neuromuscular_training.title: Neuromuscular training concepts
neuromuscular_training.description: Neuromuscular training focuses on improving the connection between the nervous system and muscles to enhance strength, coordination, and overall performance.

areas.strength: Neuromuscular training enhances muscle strength and coordination, improving physical performance.
areas.cardioFitness: This training supports cardiovascular fitness by improving endurance and oxygen utilization during physical activity.
areas.nervousSystem: Neuromuscular training strengthens the communication between the nervous system and muscles, optimizing movement efficiency.

creatine_atp_strength.title: Creatine
creatine_atp_strength.description: Creatine is a naturally occurring compound that supports ATP production, the primary energy source for muscle contractions and brain function. It enhances strength, power output, mental clarity, and muscle recovery during intense training.

areas.strength: Creatine increases phosphocreatine stores in muscles, enhancing ATP production and improving strength and power output during high-intensity exercise.
areas.energy: Creatine supports cellular energy production by replenishing ATP more rapidly, sustaining energy during intense physical activity.
areas.cardioFitness: Creatine may support cardiovascular endurance by improving oxygen utilization and reducing fatigue during sustained aerobic activities.
areas.mind: Creatine supports brain energy metabolism and cognitive function, improving mental clarity, focus, and memory.

creatine_atp_strength.warning: Creatine supplementation may affect kidney function in individuals with pre-existing conditions.

betaalanine_endurance.title: Beta-alanine for endurance
betaalanine_endurance.description: Beta-alanine is a non-essential amino acid that increases carnosine levels in muscles, buffering lactic acid and delaying fatigue during high-intensity exercise. It's particularly effective for activities lasting 1-4 minutes.

areas.strength: Beta-alanine increases muscle carnosine levels, reducing fatigue and improving performance during high-intensity exercise.
areas.cardioFitness: By buffering lactic acid, beta-alanine extends endurance capacity and allows for longer, more intense cardiovascular training sessions.

shilajit_performance.title: Shilajit for performance
shilajit_performance.description: Shilajit is a mineral-rich substance found in the Himalayas that supports mitochondrial function, enhances energy production, and improves physical performance. It contains fulvic acid and over 85 minerals in ionic form.

areas.strength: Shilajit supports muscle recovery, reduces exercise-induced muscle damage, and enhances strength and endurance.
areas.energy: Shilajit boosts mitochondrial ATP production, increasing cellular energy and reducing fatigue during physical activity.
areas.cardioFitness: Shilajit improves oxygen utilization and cardiovascular efficiency, enhancing aerobic capacity and endurance performance.

probiotics_microbiota.title: Probiotics and gut microbiota
probiotics_microbiota.description: Probiotics are beneficial bacteria that support gut health, strengthen the immune system, and improve nutrient absorption. A healthy gut microbiome is essential for overall health, mood regulation, and disease prevention.

areas.digestiveHealth: Probiotics restore and maintain healthy gut bacteria balance, improving digestion, reducing bloating, and supporting intestinal barrier function.
areas.immuneSupport: About 70% of the immune system resides in the gut. Probiotics strengthen immune function, reduce inflammation, and protect against pathogens.

yogurt.name: Yogurt
yogurt.details: 200 ml live-culture yogurt delivers roughly 5-10 billion CFU.

kefir.name: Kefir
kefir.details: 200 ml kefir offers about 10-20 billion CFU with diverse strains.

sauerkraut.name: Sauerkraut
sauerkraut.details: Half a cup raw sauerkraut (~70 g) supplies live lactic acid bacteria.

kimchi.name: Kimchi
kimchi.details: Half a cup kimchi (~85 g) provides probiotics plus prebiotic vegetables.

miso.name: Miso
miso.details: One tablespoon miso stirred into warm (not boiling) broth preserves enzymes.

lactobacillus_reuteri.title: Lactobacillus reuteri
lactobacillus_reuteri.description: Lactobacillus reuteri is a probiotic bacterial strain studied for gut balance, immune signaling, support of the intestinal barrier, and parts of oral health. Effects are strain-specific, but certain L. reuteri strains may help reduce digestive discomfort, support a more resilient gut ecosystem, and potentially contribute to a healthier oral microbiome linked to lower caries risk and better gum balance.

areas.digestiveHealth: L. reuteri may support gut barrier function, reduce microbial imbalance, and help with bloating or digestive discomfort in some people.
areas.immuneSupport: By interacting with the gut immune system, L. reuteri may help support more balanced immune signaling and lower excessive inflammatory tone. Some strains are also studied for oral immune balance and reduced growth of bacteria associated with caries and gum irritation.

fiber_microbiome.title: Fiber and microbiome health
fiber_microbiome.description: Dietary fiber acts as a prebiotic, feeding beneficial gut bacteria and supporting a healthy microbiome. Start by reaching 25 g of total fiber per day through a variety of plant foods.

areas.digestiveHealth: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements, feeds beneficial bacteria, and supports gut barrier integrity by producing short-chain fatty acids.
areas.immuneSupport: A fiber-rich diet strengthens the gut microbiome, which produces metabolites that regulate immune function and reduce systemic inflammation.
areas.longevity: Fiber intake supports butyrate production and lower low-grade inflammation, two central mechanisms linked to healthier aging.

oats.name: Oats and barley
oats.details: Half a cup dry rolled oats (~40 g) gives around 4 g beta-glucan fiber.

legumes.name: Legumes (lentils, chickpeas, beans)
legumes.details: 1 cup cooked beans or lentils (~180 g) supplies about 15 g fiber.

chiaSeeds.name: Chia or flax seeds
chiaSeeds.details: Two tablespoons chia seeds (~28 g) deliver roughly 10 g fiber.

berries.name: Berries
berries.details: 1 cup raspberries (~120 g) provides about 8 g fiber.

cruciferousVeg.name: Cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, Brussels sprouts)
cruciferousVeg.details: 1 cup steamed broccoli or cauliflower (~150 g) offers around 5 g fiber.

fiber_butyrate.title: Fermentable fiber and butyrate
fiber_butyrate.description: Fermentable fibers are broken down by gut bacteria into short-chain fatty acids, especially butyrate. Butyrate is the primary fuel for colon cells and a key regulator of gut inflammation. Aim for 30 g total fiber with at least 15 g fermentable.

areas.digestiveHealth: Resistant starch and inulin are fermented by Faecalibacterium and Roseburia to produce butyrate, which strengthens the gut lining and reduces inflammation.
areas.immuneSupport: Butyrate regulates T-cell differentiation and intestinal immune tolerance, reducing risk of inflammatory responses.
areas.longevity: Higher butyrate production is linked to reduced intestinal permeability, lower systemic inflammation, and healthier aging.

oats.name: Oats
oats.details: Half a cup dry oats (~40 g) provides roughly 4 g beta-glucan, fueling butyrate-producing bacteria.

legumes.name: Legumes (chickpeas, lentils, beans)
legumes.details: 1 cup cooked legumes (~180 g) delivers 8-15 g fermentable fiber including resistant starch and GOS.

greenBanana.name: Green (unripe) banana
greenBanana.details: One medium green banana (~120 g) contains 5-6 g resistant starch, which drops sharply on ripening.

chicoryRoot.name: Chicory root and Jerusalem artichoke
chicoryRoot.details: 100 g chicory root supplies 35-40 g inulin and FOS, among the richest sources of fermentable fiber.

cookedCooledPotato.name: Cooked and cooled potato or rice
cookedCooledPotato.details: Cooling cooked starchy foods overnight increases resistant starch content by 2-4 g per 100 g.

fiber_gel_forming_focus.title: Gel-forming fiber focus
fiber_gel_forming_focus.description: Gel-forming fibers absorb water and create viscosity in the gut. Their most important cardiometabolic effect is lowering blood lipids, especially LDL cholesterol, partly by binding bile acids and increasing cholesterol excretion. Aim for 30 g total fiber and at least 10 g gel-forming fiber daily.

areas.digestiveHealth: Gel-forming fibers such as beta-glucans, pectin, psyllium, and mucilage improve stool quality and support gut barrier function.
areas.immuneSupport: By improving lipid metabolism and gut-derived inflammatory tone, gel-forming fibers can support better immune regulation.
areas.longevity: Higher intake of viscous gel-forming fibers is consistently associated with lower LDL cholesterol, improved cardiometabolic markers, and better long-term health outcomes.

oats.name: Oats and barley
oats.details: Beta-glucans in oats and barley are classic gel-forming fibers with well-documented LDL-lowering effects.

psylliumHusk.name: Psyllium husk
psylliumHusk.details: 1 tablespoon psyllium (~9 g) is rich in gel-forming fiber and is one of the most effective dietary tools to lower LDL cholesterol.

chiaSeeds.name: Chia seeds
chiaSeeds.details: Chia forms a mucilage gel in contact with water and contributes both total and gel-forming fiber.

apples.name: Apples
apples.details: Apples are rich in pectin, a gel-forming fiber associated with better stool consistency and microbiome support.

okra.name: Okra
okra.details: Okra contains mucilage and pectin that contribute to gel formation and gut comfort.

fiber_non_gel_forming_focus.title: Non-gel-forming fiber focus
fiber_non_gel_forming_focus.description: Non-gel-forming fibers are bulk-forming structural fibers that increase stool mass and speed colonic transit. This is important because shorter transit time reduces how long the gut lining is exposed to potentially harmful breakdown products and supports regular bowel emptying. Aim for 30 g total fiber and around 20 g non-gel-forming fiber daily.

areas.digestiveHealth: Cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, and arabinoxylan support bowel regularity by adding stool bulk and reducing transit time, lowering constipation risk and bloating.
areas.immuneSupport: Regular bowel transit may reduce local inflammatory pressure by limiting mucosal contact with irritating residues, supporting a healthier gut environment for immune balance.
areas.longevity: Consistent intake of structural fibers supports long-term bowel function, healthier transit patterns, and lower risk patterns linked to colorectal disease.

wheatBran.name: Wheat bran
wheatBran.details: Wheat bran is rich in arabinoxylan and insoluble fibers that efficiently increase stool bulk.

cruciferousVeg.name: Cruciferous vegetables
cruciferousVeg.details: Broccoli, cabbage, and Brussels sprouts contribute cellulose and hemicellulose.

leafyGreens.name: Leafy greens
leafyGreens.details: Leafy greens provide insoluble structural fibers that support bowel movement regularity.

nuts.name: Nuts and seeds
nuts.details: Nuts contribute cellulose and lignin, helping increase stool mass and satiety.

wholeGrainRye.name: Whole-grain rye
wholeGrainRye.details: Whole rye products contain arabinoxylan-rich bran fractions that support regular transit.

plant_diversity_30_week.title: 30 different plants per week
plant_diversity_30_week.description: Aim for at least 30 different plant foods per week (vegetables, berries, fruits, legumes, nuts, seeds, herbs, and whole grains). Higher plant diversity is linked to a more diverse and resilient microbiome. How to fulfill it: count each unique plant once per week, and use mixed meals to increase variety fast.

areas.digestiveHealth: A wider range of plant fibers and polyphenols feeds more microbial species, which can improve stool quality, gut barrier support, and digestive resilience.
areas.immuneSupport: Greater microbiome diversity is associated with better immune signaling balance and lower chronic inflammatory tone.
areas.longevity: Weekly plant diversity is linked to better metabolic and inflammatory profiles, both relevant for healthy aging.

legumes.name: Build around legumes
legumes.details: Use 2-3 different legumes weekly (for example lentils, chickpeas, black beans). Each counts as one unique plant.

berries.name: Use mixed berries and fruit
berries.details: Rotate berry and fruit types across the week. Frozen mixes are an easy way to add 3-5 unique plants quickly.

leafyGreens.name: Rotate leafy greens
leafyGreens.details: Swap between spinach, kale, arugula, romaine, and herbs instead of repeating one green every day.

nuts.name: Mix nuts and seeds
nuts.details: Use mixed nuts/seeds (for example walnuts, almonds, pumpkin seeds, chia) and count each type separately.

freshHerbs.name: Treat herbs as plants that count
freshHerbs.details: Parsley, dill, cilantro, basil, mint, and similar herbs all count toward the weekly 30 target.

fish_omega3_weekly.title: Fish meals for omega-3 and heart health
fish_omega3_weekly.description: Aim for 3 fish meals per week, with at least 1 fatty fish meal rich in EPA and DHA omega-3 fats. Omega-3 fatty acids support cardiovascular health, reduce inflammation, and promote brain function. Fatty fish like salmon, mackerel, and sardines are the most bioavailable sources.

areas.cardioFitness: Omega-3 fats reduce triglycerides, support healthy blood pressure, and improve endothelial function for cardiovascular resilience.
areas.brainHealth: EPA and DHA are structural components of brain cell membranes and support cognitive function, mood regulation, and neuroprotection.
areas.inflammation: Omega-3 fats actively reduce systemic inflammation by modulating immune signaling and shifting the inflammatory balance toward resolution.

fattyFish.name: Fatty fish (salmon, mackerel, sardines, herring, trout)
fattyFish.details: 100 g wild salmon provides ~2 g EPA+DHA; mackerel provides ~1.5 g per 100 g. Highest bioavailable omega-3 sources.

leanFish.name: Lean fish (cod, haddock, flounder)
leanFish.details: 100 g provides ~0.2 g omega-3s. Excellent protein source and easier to prepare than fatty fish.

canTuna.name: Canned fish (sardines, mackerel)
canTuna.details: Convenient option with similar omega-3 content to fresh fish. Often packed in oil for added omega-3s.

preparation.name: Best preparation methods
preparation.details: Baking, steaming, or poaching preserve omega-3s. Frying at high heat can damage delicate fats; use moderate heat or eat raw (sushi).

quantity.name: Portion recommendation
quantity.details: 120–150 g fish meal (roughly a palm-sized fillet) provides meaningful omega-3 intake. Higher frequency compensates for smaller portions.

polyphenol_microbiome.title: Polyphenols and microbiome health
polyphenol_microbiome.description: Polyphenols are plant compounds that act as prebiotics, selectively feeding beneficial gut bacteria. A high polyphenol intake supports microbiome diversity, reduces gut inflammation, and protects against oxidative stress.

areas.digestiveHealth: Polyphenols are partially metabolized by gut bacteria, producing bioactive metabolites that protect the gut lining and support microbiome balance.
areas.immuneSupport: Polyphenol metabolites regulate immune signaling and reduce systemic inflammation through interactions with the gut-immune axis.
areas.longevity: Higher polyphenol intake is associated with lower oxidative damage, reduced inflammation, and improved markers of healthy aging.

berries.name: Berries (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries)
berries.details: 1 cup blueberries (~150 g) provides roughly 400–600 mg polyphenols including anthocyanins.

darkChocolate.name: Dark chocolate (70–85% cacao)
darkChocolate.details: 30 g dark chocolate supplies approximately 200–400 mg polyphenols, mainly flavanols and catechins.

pomegranate.name: Pomegranate
pomegranate.details: Half a pomegranate (~150 g) contains around 400 mg polyphenols including ellagitannins.

greenTea.name: Green tea
greenTea.details: 2 cups green tea (~500 ml) provides about 200–400 mg catechins and other flavonoids.

extraVirginOliveOil.name: Extra virgin olive oil (EVOO)
extraVirginOliveOil.details: 2 tablespoons EVOO (~30 ml) supply roughly 30–50 mg polyphenols including oleocanthal.

milk_thistle_liver.title: Milk thistle for liver health
milk_thistle_liver.description: Milk thistle contains silymarin, a powerful antioxidant that protects liver cells, supports detoxification, and promotes liver regeneration. It's particularly beneficial for liver health and digestive function.

areas.digestiveHealth: Milk thistle supports bile production and liver function, improving fat digestion and overall digestive health.
areas.immuneSupport: By supporting liver detoxification, milk thistle reduces toxic burden on the body and strengthens overall immune resilience.

hiit_vo2max.title: HIIT for VO2 max
hiit_vo2max.description: High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) is one of the most effective methods to improve VO2 max, the maximum amount of oxygen your body can use during exercise. Unlike Zone 2, which mainly builds more capillaries and more mitochondria, HIIT strongly improves how efficiently your existing mitochondria work under high demand.

areas.cardioFitness: HIIT training significantly increases VO2 max, improving cardiovascular capacity, endurance, and overall aerobic fitness.
areas.energy: HIIT improves the working capacity of existing mitochondria and the ability to generate energy rapidly at high intensity, increasing metabolic efficiency when demand is high.
areas.longevity: Higher VO2 max is one of the strongest predictors of long-term health and survival, making HIIT a valuable longevity stimulus when recovery is managed well.

vo2max_4x4_intervals.title: VO2max 4x4 intervals
vo2max_4x4_intervals.description: A classic protocol for improving VO2 max is 4 x 4 minutes at high but controlled intensity (about 85-95% of max heart rate), with 3 minutes easy recovery between intervals. Performed 1-2 times per week, this can effectively raise oxygen uptake capacity, stroke volume, and performance.

areas.cardioFitness: 4x4 intervals provide a strong central cardiovascular stimulus and are one of the most evidence-based methods for increasing VO2 max.
areas.energy: Improved oxygen delivery and utilization supports higher sustainable output and better energetic capacity in daily life.
areas.longevity: Maintaining high aerobic capacity over time is closely associated with healthier aging and lower cardiometabolic risk.

vo2max_hill_intervals.title: Hill intervals for VO2 max
vo2max_hill_intervals.description: Uphill intervals (for example 6-10 repeats of 45-90 seconds) are an efficient way to improve VO2 max while also building lower-body strength and running economy. Hills reduce impact speed while increasing force demand, making them a practical high-intensity option.

areas.cardioFitness: Hill intervals challenge oxygen transport and heart-lung capacity, supporting improvements in VO2 max and endurance performance.
areas.strength: Uphill work increases force production in glutes, calves, and posterior chain, improving strength-endurance transfer.
areas.longevity: Combining aerobic intensity and musculoskeletal loading supports both cardiovascular resilience and functional capacity with age.

running_volume_aerobic.title: Running volume for aerobic capacity
running_volume_aerobic.description: Running volume is about the total amount of running you accumulate over a week. In practice, a large share of that volume should still be done in Zone 2, otherwise the total stress can become too high for recovery, joints, and the nervous system. Unlike Zone 2, which mainly describes the intensity of an individual session, running volume is more about building durability, tissue tolerance, and aerobic capacity through consistent total workload over time. When increased gradually, it can also strengthen tendons, ligaments, and tissue tolerance around the joints.

areas.cardioFitness: Regular running volume strengthens the heart, increases stroke volume, and improves overall cardiovascular endurance and aerobic capacity.
areas.energy: Aerobic running improves fat oxidation, enhances mitochondrial function, and increases sustained energy levels for daily activities.

zone2_slow_running.title: Zone 2 / slow running
zone2_slow_running.description: Easy Zone 2 running is one of the most useful health habits because it gives you a large cardio-metabolic return without excessive stress. The goal is not speed or mileage, but a relaxed pace where you can still speak in full sentences. Zone 2 increases the number of capillaries feeding the muscles and stimulates the creation of more mitochondria, making muscles better at receiving oxygen and producing aerobic energy. This is different from running volume: Zone 2 is primarily about keeping effort easy enough, while running volume is about how much total running you accumulate over time.

areas.cardioFitness: Slow Zone 2 running strengthens the heart and increases capillary density in working muscles, improving oxygen delivery and aerobic endurance.
areas.energy: Easy aerobic movement stimulates the creation of more mitochondria and improves day-to-day energy with relatively low strain.

multivitamin_general.title: Multivitamin
multivitamin_general.description: A multivitamin provides essential vitamins and minerals that support overall health, energy, and vitality. It can help fill nutritional gaps in the diet.

areas.energy: Multivitamins support energy production by providing B-vitamins and minerals necessary for cellular metabolism.
areas.immuneSupport: Vitamins and minerals in multivitamins strengthen the immune system and help the body defend against infections.

magnesium.title: Magnesium
magnesium.description: Magnesium is an essential mineral that plays a vital role in muscle relaxation, nervous system function, and sleep quality. It helps the body regulate stress hormones and promotes deeper, more restorative sleep.

areas.sleepQuality: Magnesium improves sleep quality by regulating melatonin and promoting muscle relaxation.
areas.nervousSystem: Magnesium supports the nervous system by regulating neurotransmitters and reducing stress.
areas.energy: Magnesium is necessary for energy production and reduces fatigue by supporting ATP synthesis.

leafyGreens.name: Dark leafy greens (spinach, chard, kale)
leafyGreens.details: 1 cup cooked spinach (~180 g) provides about 150 mg magnesium.

pumpkinSeeds.name: Pumpkin or sunflower seeds
pumpkinSeeds.details: 30 g roasted pumpkin seeds give around 150 mg magnesium.

almonds.name: Almonds and other nuts
almonds.details: 30 g almonds contribute roughly 80 mg magnesium.

darkChocolate.name: Dark chocolate (70-85% cacao)
darkChocolate.details: 30 g 70-85% cacao dark chocolate supplies about 65 mg magnesium.

blackBeans.name: Black beans, chickpeas, or lentils
blackBeans.details: 1 cup cooked black beans (~170 g) yields about 120 mg magnesium.

avocado.name: Avocado
avocado.details: One medium avocado offers roughly 60 mg magnesium.

zinc_comprehensive_support.title: Zinc for immune resilience
zinc_comprehensive_support.description: Zinc is a trace mineral critical for immune defense, tissue repair, hormone balance, and normal hair growth. Highly absorbable forms can help maintain resilience during stress and intense training, and low zinc status can contribute to hair shedding and poorer hair quality.

areas.immuneSupport: Zinc supports innate and adaptive immunity by regulating cytokine signaling and white blood cell activity.
areas.nervousSystem: Adequate zinc helps maintain neurotransmitter balance, supporting mood and stress tolerance.
areas.energy: Zinc is required for hundreds of enzymatic reactions linked to energy metabolism and recovery.

oysters.name: Oysters
oysters.details: Three medium oysters deliver about 30 mg zinc.

beef.name: Beef and lamb
beef.details: A 120 g portion of beef provides roughly 5 mg zinc.

pumpkinSeeds.name: Pumpkin seeds
pumpkinSeeds.details: 30 g pumpkin seeds add about 2-3 mg zinc.

chickpeas.name: Chickpeas and lentils
chickpeas.details: 1 cup cooked chickpeas (~170 g) gives around 2.5 mg zinc.

cashews.name: Cashews
cashews.details: 30 g cashews supply roughly 1.6 mg zinc.

selenium_thyroid_antioxidant.title: Selenium for thyroid and antioxidant defense
selenium_thyroid_antioxidant.description: Selenium powers glutathione-based antioxidant enzymes and supports the conversion of thyroid hormones, helping maintain immunity, energy, stress tolerance, and normal hair growth. Low selenium status or impaired thyroid function can negatively affect hair quality.

areas.immuneSupport: Selenium supports antibody production and regulates inflammation, bolstering immune resilience.
areas.energy: Selenium-dependent enzymes activate thyroid hormones that drive metabolic energy and mitochondrial efficiency.
areas.nervousSystem: Selenium protects neurons from oxidative stress and supports balanced mood and stress responses.

brazilNuts.name: Brazil nuts
brazilNuts.details: One Brazil nut delivers 60-90 mcg selenium; limit to 1-2 per day.

sardines.name: Sardines and salmon
sardines.details: 100 g sardines provide about 45 mcg selenium.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.details: Two eggs supply roughly 28 mcg selenium.

shiitakeMushrooms.name: Shiitake mushrooms
shiitakeMushrooms.details: 100 g cooked shiitake mushrooms give around 20 mcg selenium.

sunflowerSeeds.name: Sunflower seeds
sunflowerSeeds.details: 30 g sunflower seeds add about 18 mcg selenium.

iodine_thyroid_balance.title: Iodine for thyroid balance
iodine_thyroid_balance.description: Iodine supplies the raw material for thyroid hormones, helping maintain metabolic drive, immune resilience, clear thinking, and normal hair growth. When thyroid function is suboptimal, hair density and hair quality often suffer.

areas.energy: Adequate iodine keeps T3 and T4 production robust, sustaining metabolic energy throughout the day.
areas.immuneSupport: Balanced thyroid hormones modulate immune signaling and help the body respond appropriately to stressors.
areas.nervousSystem: Iodine supports nervous system stability by maintaining hormone balance that affects mood, focus, and thermoregulation.

seaweed.name: Seaweed (kombu, nori, wakame)
seaweed.details: One 5 g sheet of dried seaweed can supply 150-300 mcg iodine; use sparingly.

iodizedSalt.name: Iodized salt
iodizedSalt.details: Half a teaspoon of iodized salt provides close to 150 mcg iodine.

dairy.name: Dairy products
dairy.details: A 250 ml glass of milk or yogurt delivers about 50 mcg iodine.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.details: Two eggs provide roughly 50 mcg iodine.

cod.name: Cod and other white fish
cod.details: A 120 g cod fillet offers about 110 mcg iodine.

betaine_cardiovascular.title: Betaine
betaine_cardiovascular.description: Betaine supports cardiovascular function and physical performance.

ashwagandha_adaptogen.title: Ashwagandha
ashwagandha_adaptogen.description: Ashwagandha is an adaptogenic herb traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine. It helps the body manage stress by supporting cortisol balance and promoting relaxation.

areas.nervousSystem: Ashwagandha supports the nervous system by reducing stress and promoting calm through cortisol regulation.
areas.energy: Ashwagandha helps combat fatigue and supports sustained energy levels throughout the day.
areas.immuneSupport: Ashwagandha has immune-modulating properties that support overall immune health.

rhodiola_adaptogen.title: Rhodiola
rhodiola_adaptogen.description: Rhodiola is an adaptogenic herb known for enhancing mental and physical performance. It helps the body adapt to stress and supports cognitive function.

areas.nervousSystem: Rhodiola supports the nervous system by reducing mental fatigue and improving stress resilience.
areas.energy: Rhodiola enhances physical endurance and reduces fatigue during demanding activities.
areas.mind: Rhodiola improves cognitive function, focus, and mental clarity, especially under stress.

holy_basil_adaptogen.title: Holy Basil (Tulsi)
holy_basil_adaptogen.description: Holy Basil, also known as Tulsi, is an adaptogenic herb revered in traditional medicine for its stress-reducing and immune-supporting properties.

areas.nervousSystem: Holy Basil helps calm the nervous system and reduce stress through its adaptogenic effects.
areas.immuneSupport: Holy Basil supports immune function with its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties.

reishi_mushroom.title: Reishi
reishi_mushroom.description: Reishi is a medicinal mushroom commonly used to support immune balance, recovery, and a calmer nervous system.

areas.immuneSupport: Reishi may support immune balance through beta-glucans and other immune-modulating compounds.
areas.nervousSystem: Reishi is often used to promote calm, stress resilience, and nervous system recovery.

lions_mane_mushroom.title: Lion's Mane
lions_mane_mushroom.description: Lion's Mane is a medicinal mushroom best known for supporting the brain, focus, and nervous system function.

areas.mind: Lion's Mane may support focus, mental clarity, and cognitive performance.
areas.nervousSystem: It is being studied for its potential to support nerve repair and neurotrophic signaling.

chaga_mushroom.title: Chaga
chaga_mushroom.description: Chaga is an antioxidant-rich medicinal mushroom traditionally used to support immune health and cellular protection.

areas.immuneSupport: Chaga contains polyphenols and other compounds that may help support a more resilient immune system.
areas.energy: By helping reduce oxidative stress, Chaga may indirectly support energy and recovery.

cordyceps_adaptogen.title: Cordyceps
cordyceps_adaptogen.description: Cordyceps is a medicinal mushroom known for its energy-boosting and performance-enhancing properties. It supports cellular energy production and endurance.

areas.energy: Cordyceps enhances cellular energy production by supporting mitochondrial function and ATP generation.
areas.cardioFitness: Cordyceps improves oxygen utilization and cardiovascular endurance during physical activity.
areas.immuneSupport: Cordyceps has immune-modulating effects that support overall immune health.

zone2_mitochondrial_base.title: Zone 2 for a mitochondrial base
zone2_mitochondrial_base.description: Zone 2 training builds your aerobic foundation by increasing mitochondrial density, capillarization, and fat oxidation. In practice, that means more capillaries feeding the muscles and more mitochondria inside the muscle cells. The goal is a steady, conversational pace where you can speak in full sentences and keep intensity stable over time.

areas.cardioFitness: Zone 2 improves aerobic capacity through increased stroke volume, higher capillary density, and more efficient oxygen delivery to working muscles.
areas.energy: Consistent Zone 2 supports mitochondrial biogenesis, meaning the creation of more mitochondria, and improves energy metabolism for more sustainable energy during training and daily life.
areas.longevity: Maintaining aerobic base and mitochondrial function is strongly linked to healthier aging, higher resilience, and better long-term physical capacity.

zone2_mitochondrial_base.analyzePrompt: Analyze the user's training pattern and determine whether they have enough low-intensity aerobic volume (Zone 2) to support mitochondrial development.

fascia_strength_whole_body_variation.title: 4-5 training modalities for whole-body fascia strength
fascia_strength_whole_body_variation.description: For long-term resilience, avoid repeating only one training pattern. Aim for at least 4-5 different activity types each week, for example: strength, Zone 2 cardio, impact/plyometric loading, rotational or unilateral work, and mobility/balance. This creates varied mechanical signals that support fascia quality, tendon and ligament tolerance, bone remodeling, and whole-body muscle function.

areas.longevity: Training variety across the week helps preserve movement capacity, connective tissue quality, and functional independence as you age.
areas.strength: Different loading patterns improve force transfer through fascia and build stronger, more resilient muscles, tendons, ligaments, and bones.
areas.nervousSystem: Changing training stimulus improves coordination and motor adaptability while reducing repetitive stress on the nervous system.

fasted_aerobic_training.title: Fasted aerobic training
fasted_aerobic_training.description: Low-intensity training with low glycogen availability (e.g., before breakfast) can stimulate fat metabolism and mitochondrial adaptations. Use selectively and primarily in Zone 2 — not for hard intervals.

areas.energy: Training with low glycogen availability may improve fat oxidation and stimulate mitochondrial signaling pathways linked to endurance adaptation.
areas.cardioFitness: When kept low intensity, this can improve aerobic robustness without compromising quality in high-intensity sessions when periodized correctly.

lactate_threshold_training.title: Threshold training for 10K–10 miles
lactate_threshold_training.description: Threshold training (tempo just below lactate threshold) makes you faster without accumulating fatigue as quickly. It’s a key driver for 10K and longer races because you can sustain a high pace with controlled effort.

areas.cardioFitness: Threshold sessions raise the pace you can sustain before lactate accumulates too quickly, improving race performance over 5–10K distances.
areas.energy: Improved lactate clearance and more efficient energy systems let you produce more work with less perceived fatigue at higher speeds.
areas.mind: Lactate have neurological effects that can improve focus and mental toughness during hard efforts, helping you push through. It also has neuroprotective effects that may support brain health and resilience under stress.

lactate_threshold_training.analyzePrompt: Analyze the user's current fitness and recommend a threshold structure (e.g., 20–40 minutes continuous or broken into blocks) that matches their capacity.

running_economy_drills.title: Running economy: technique, drills, and strides
running_economy_drills.description: Running economy is how little energy you need for a given pace. Short technique drills and strides (brief controlled accelerations) improve neuromuscular efficiency so you can run faster at the same effort.

areas.strength: Strides and drills improve force application and elastic recoil, making your stride more efficient and feel ‘lighter’.
areas.nervousSystem: Short speed exposures train coordination and muscle fiber recruitment, improving movement efficiency.
areas.cardioFitness: Better running economy lowers the oxygen cost at a given pace, improving endurance performance.

stride_frequency_optimization.title: Cadence and stride frequency
